title: Isolated hostile-test lane infrastructure
description: Objective: provide one shell-neutral, typechecked root runner for fault and security suites without letting broad root Vitest discovery or zero-case sweeps create false evidence. Deliverable: root `test:fault` and `test:security` scripts, dedicated `tests/fault` and `tests/security` tsconfig/Vitest configs, and a non-authority security lane smoke case; existing Foundation fault tests prove the fault lane is non-empty. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: package.json has no test:fault/test:security scripts, only tests/fault/foundation has its own tsconfig and three `.test.ts` cases, tests/security is absent, and task-05ce9b8f comments describe but did not create G0. NOT in scope: adding security/fault schedules, editing tests/fault/foundation/**, disaster/Linux/macOS subtrees, reimplementing production authority, or claiming any platform/security scenario PASS. Hard dependencies/serialization: wait until package.json owners task-739879d0d1ce4a7ea4d1430688cdc4dc and task-9449ce65fae544ef9809691ec079f599 finish and reconcile their scripts. Consumers: task-05ce9b8f982f448a9cdaa4142a653f32, task-0c89476b78044024b07c86c0c8986bd0, task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275, and task-e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856. Owned paths: package.json, tests/fault/tsconfig.json, tests/fault/vitest.config.ts, tests/security/tsconfig.json, tests/security/vitest.config.ts, tests/security/lane-smoke.security.ts. Verification: pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security.
definitionOfDone: `package.json` exposes shell-neutral `test:fault` and `test:security` commands that each run `tsc -p` for its own tree before Vitest with its own config, preserving all foreign scripts added by serialized predecessor tasks.

The fault config discovers existing `tests/fault/foundation/**/*.test.ts` plus future `**/*.fault.ts`; the security config discovers `**/*.security.ts`; both set `passWithNoTests:false`, deterministic serial execution, and exclude the other lane.

The committed security lane smoke case tests only runner/config facts and grants no product authority; each lane run reports at least one collected file/case, and a zero-case or type-error lane exits non-zero.

The root `pnpm test` behavior remains explicit: hostile-only `.fault.ts`/`.security.ts` files are not accidentally counted as ordinary regression evidence, while existing Foundation `.test.ts` behavior is preserved.
Fresh `pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security` exits 0 on Windows and uses no Unix-only shell commands; config path normalization is portable to macOS/Linux.
